Images 1, 2 and 3 are FIXTURE AND STYLE BIBLES — flat elevations of the three walls in this shot: the left wall with the doorway and the server rack, the far wall with the desk, and the right wall with the television and the dartboard. Preserve their drawing style, line weight, paper colour, palette, and the exact design of every fixture. Do NOT copy their flat orthographic camera.
Image 4 is the COMPOSITION ROUGH for the target camera. Follow its camera, perspective, horizon and left-to-right placement exactly; replace each grey block with the corresponding fixture; remove every guide mark and every green block — the green blocks mark where people will stand and are NOT drawn.

CAMERA: a very wide shot of the WHOLE office drawn as a cutaway, the way a cartoon shows a room with its near wall taken away: the lens stands outside the room where the missing near wall would be, a little above a standing person's eye level, tipped slightly down, and sees all three remaining walls at once. The far wall faces us across the full width of the frame; the left wall and the right wall run away from us towards it; the ceiling line runs along the top of the frame and the floor is a broad plane filling the lower half. There is no wall between the camera and the room.

PERSPECTIVE — draw it deliberately. The vanishing point sits on the far wall at its centre, at eye height. The left and right walls converge towards it: fixtures on the left wall show their RIGHT-HAND faces, fixtures on the right wall show their LEFT-HAND faces, and both shrink as they recede. Two clean vertical corner seams run floor to ceiling where the far wall meets the side walls. The two side baseboards slope towards the far wall's level baseboard. Vertical lines stay vertical. Nearer fixtures are drawn larger; the far wall's fixtures are the smallest.

THE ROOM IS WRECKED AND AT REST. VISIBLE. Along the LEFT wall, near to far: a water cooler with paper cups; a low coffee counter with a drip machine, jug and mugs, and above it a wide flat screen popped out of the black server rack on an arm, its face full of dense rows of small dark dashes and blocks like code, cabling spilling from the rack; the tall black server rack; a plain open empty doorway; a squared-away shelf of ring binders; and at the far corner three enormous towers of loose paper fringed with hundreds of small coloured sticky flags rising from the floor right out of the top of the frame, with loose sheets heaped around their feet and over a small supply desk. On the FAR wall, left to right: a tall grey filing cabinet with boxes and a plant on top; a low printer bench with a wire paper tray and, above it, a whiteboard of half-erased diagrams; the long wooden desk in the centre with THREE monitors showing quiet lines of code, a desk lamp and a mug, the cork board of pinned notes above it and the shelf of binders with a trailing plant, and an empty office chair pulled up to the desk with its back to us; a small brass bell on a wall bracket with a pull cord; the fat striped confetti cannon lying toppled on its side beside its fallen tripod, streamers and confetti scattered over the desk and the floor around the chair; and a low storage bench with boxes. Along the RIGHT wall, far to near: at the far corner a ragged hole smashed through the wall with blank cream paper beyond it, plaster rubble, broken laths and an overturned round side table spilled across the floor, a big cardboard rocket leaning out of the hole nose-up, and a dartboard with darts stuck in the wall around it; stacked crates; tall binder shelving; a low credenza with, high above it, an old boxy television on a bracket shelf, its screen lit pale with a jagged falling line on it; and at the near end, small square sketches of shopping bags, buttons and little round creatures taped over the wall and drifting across the floor in overlapping piles. Loose sheets of paper lie flat across the whole floor.

OUT OF FRAME: the wall of taped sketches, the string lights, the worktable and the storage cabinet — everything on the removed near wall.
The room is empty of characters and people. The chair is empty.

Warm cream drawing paper throughout, a pale putty cream, never white and never yellow. The floor is the same cream a half-step darker. Walls and floor are flat, quiet, and low-contrast — the room is a pale ground, and colour lives only on small props. Graphite line and cross-hatch shadow carry all the form. Overall value stays high-key and even: no dark corners, no pooled shadow, no colour cast, no vignette, no dramatic lighting.

Hand-drawn animation pencil test: graphite line, visible construction lines, cross-hatch shadow, light coloured-pencil wash on props only, paper tooth showing — no flat vector fill, no digital gradients, no painterly rendering, no photographic lighting, no 3D. Do not add any text.
